question: Is North Sister Southeast Ridge distinct from our South Ridge, and if so what is its row?
answer: Distinct lower line, same finish. The SE ridge is climbed from Pole Creek via the Soap Creek trail, then cross-country west to the ridge base at ~7,800 ft, ~2,000 ft of loose ridge to pinnacles at ~9,800 ft, passed on their west side into the Bowling Alley, which is also the final obstacle of the South Ridge. The South Ridge instead goes up the Hayden Glacier to the Middle-North saddle (~9,000 ft) and follows the ridge from there. So the two share only the summit finish. Our catalog holds only South Ridge (or_south_ridge); no SE Ridge under any name.
recommendation: Add a new route Southeast Ridge on or_north_sister; keep South Ridge unchanged. Trailhead is the same Pole Creek pin already proposed (44.18754,-121.70081).

proposed.name: Southeast Ridge
proposed.overview: A long, loose scree-and-rock ridge on the southeast side of North Sister that is often chosen over the northwest ridge in summer. It climbs about 2,000 ft of unstable ground to a group of pinnacles, then merges with the South Ridge finish through the Bowling Alley channel to the summit. Rockfall from your own party is the main hazard.
proposed.approach: From the Pole Creek trailhead follow the trail toward Soap Creek, then leave it and head cross-country west through forest to the base of the ridge near 7,800 ft. Navigation is by compass and terrain; there is no maintained path.
proposed.descent_text: Retrace the route: downclimb or rappel the Bowling Alley (rap slings are usually in place), skirt back around the pinnacles on their south side and descend the ridge. The scree runs down to about 7,000 ft, so gaiters help.
proposed.note: Grade 4th is inferred from the shared Bowling Alley finish; no source gave a class for the SE ridge itself.
